topics.label: Introduction to Cancer Etiology and Learning Outcomes
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic provides the framing for the lecture, introducing the lecturer, the course context, and the key learning objectives regarding cancer causation.

topics.label: Intrinsic and Hereditary Drivers of Cancer
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how cancer develops as a genetic and evolutionary process driven by endogenous metabolic errors and inherited predispositions.

topics.label: Environmental Exposures and Epidemiological Evidence
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics evaluate the role of external environmental risks in cancer development through the debate on intrinsic bad luck versus extrinsic exposure and global epidemiological variation.

topics.label: Infectious Pathogens in Cancer Development
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how infectious agents drive oncogenesis, focusing on the epidemiological and biological mechanisms linking viral and bacterial infections to malignancies like Burkitt lymphoma.

topics.label: Mechanisms of Chemical and Physical Carcinogenesis
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics detail the biochemical mechanisms by which direct mutagens, metabolically activated compounds, and inflammatory promoters induce DNA damage and tumor growth across different tissues and life stages.

topics.label: Methodologies for Detecting and Testing Carcinogens
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics outline the genomic, epidemiological, animal, and in vitro experimental strategies used to identify carcinogens and verify their mutagenic potential.

topics.label: Lecture Summary and Risk-Benefit Analysis
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic serves as the closing framing for the lecture, summarising core takeaways about environmental risks and concluding with personal and public risk-benefit considerations.
